svg.title: DC-SCI connector pin regions named in the DC-SCM 2.1 text (partial map)
svg.desc: Strip diagram of the 168-pin SFF-TA-1002 4C+ connector with A1-A70, B1-B70 and OCP bay OA1-OA14, OB1-OB14 pins, highlighting pin ranges for PCIe, eSPI, NC-SI, USB, presence, reset and clock signals.
svg.text: DC-SCI connector pin regions named in the DC-SCM 2.1 text (partial map)
PCIe x1 pairs: A30-B31 (HPM to SCM, BMC endpoint), A33-B34 (alt: BMC root complex / USB3.1), A65-B66 (usually a USB host controller)
OA2-OB12: PCIe up to Gen5 x4, HPM to endpoints on the SCM; splittable x4, 2x2, 4x1
B1-B8: eSPI (CS0/ALERT0/RESET); B9-B10: second chip-select/alert (usually ends at the HPM FPGA)
B43-B49: first NC-SI RMII-based transport interface (use this one first)
B36-B37 and B68-B69: USB lanes in the Fig. 60 example (host or managed USB)
B51: optional BMC PCIe-root-complex PERST# (otherwise sent over LTPI)
A7: PRSNT0_N and B58: PRSNT1_N presence pair (Fig. 63)
A68-A69: a PCIe reference-clock pair (section 3.5.2.1; alternate signal name when the BMC is root)
Important: this is NOT a full pinout. Only ranges explicitly stated in the specification text or figure labels are drawn.
For design work use the official DC-SCI pinout spreadsheet and the figures 48 (single node) and 49 (dual node) in the spec.
Pin counts: 2 x 70 + 2 x 14 = 168, matching the '4C+ 168' connector (4C = 140 pins, plus the 28-pin OCP bay).
Original diagram. Source: OCP DC-SCM Rev 2.1 v1.1 sections 3.1, 3.5.1-3.5.5, 3.6 and Figs. 48, 50, 56, 60, 63.
